name: Camille Corot
findings: Uses dark olive brown 1.7x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 2408 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, rinnemann's green turns up as a small accent in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 4.0x the archive's rate (from 2408 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, warbler green turns up as the lightest note in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 4.5x the archive's rate (from 2408 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, rinnemann's green turns up as the shadow in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 3.6x the archive's rate (from 2408 paintings here).
Pairs graphite violet with smoke more than chance would predict (3 of 2408 paintings here).
Pairs blackish grey with graphite grey more than chance would predict (4 of 2408 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark olive brown, dark olive grey) covers 65% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, dark olive brown to dark olive brown, smoky black.
